consequence.statement: Managed resources now operate within Kubernetes namespaces rather than cluster-wide, affecting resource organization, isolation, and cross-namespace composition patterns.

original.statement: Crossplane v2 makes all managed resources namespaced, enabling namespace-scoped resource isolation instead of cluster-wide scoping.

consequence.statement: Nothing happens if the operator does nothing. Namespaced MRs are optional, Crossplane v2 is backward compatible with v1-style cluster-scoped MRs, and new provider releases support both namespaced and cluster-scoped MRs. Cluster-scoped MRs are called a legacy feature that may be deprecated and removed at a future date, but they are not deprecated in this release.

corrected.statement: Namespaced managed resources are an opt-in Crossplane v2 feature that the upgrade guide suggests trying. Existing cluster-scoped MRs keep working because v2 is backward compatible, so doing nothing has no operational consequence.

decision.reason: [ev-914f3976650c] is only an optional "Start using v2 features" pointer to a getting-started guide. [ev-f9df8ec77b1f] says namespaced MRs are a new option, that Crossplane v2 is backward compatible with v1-style cluster-scoped MRs, and that new provider releases support both kinds. So nothing changes for an operator who does nothing, and the proposed claim that MRs "now operate within namespaces rather than cluster-wide" misreads the evidence. Removing cluster-scoped MRs is only a possible future step and is not part of this item.
